_about: One record per studio case study → studio/work-<slug>.html, built by tools/build-studio.mjs. These are GEMIS's real projects — the six client stories in scripts/cases.py / scripts/stories.py, plus ManaGEM, the product — and every line is sourced from those records, scripts/facts.md (confirmed metrics) and scripts/endorsements.md (approved quotations, copied exactly). Nothing is invented. A field the record cannot fill is null, and the page shows a review-only note (?review=1) in its place. Thumbnails are studio/assets/cases/<slug>.jpg, rendered by tools/studio-thumbs.mjs from the app windows and phones cut from the case-study videos. 'nda' is the level to agree with the client in writing before publishing: full | anonymised | results-only; 'ndaAgreed' flips to true once that is in writing.

cases.name: WasteMart
cases.timeline: Client for more than ten years; the system has grown with the business
cases.result: Six hours a week back, per depot
cases.imageAlt: WasteMart: the operations dashboard on a laptop and the driver app on a phone
problem: A business that needs its waste removed should be able to make one call. Behind that call at WasteMart sat a lot of manual work: building the quote, attaching the right terms, chasing payment, and then remembering to tell operations that a job was on.
Sales, finance and operations each held part of the picture, so proof of payment was chased, jobs were scheduled late, and nobody — including the customer — could see where an order stood.
cases.findingsNote: There is no formal research report in the record for this project. The findings are the four manual jobs that sat behind one phone call, as the work was actually done.
findings: Quotes were built by hand and the right terms attached from memory.
Payment was chased, and proof of payment waited for.
Operations found out about jobs late — only once someone remembered to tell them.
Nobody, including the customer, could see where an order stood.

changes.decision: Price the quote automatically from the service picked, with standard terms and conditions attached every time.
changes.why: A quote that cannot go out without its terms removes a class of errors and most of the time spent building it.

changes.decision: Send a secure payment link with the quote, and let payment itself trigger the next step.
changes.why: When payment drives the schedule there is nothing to chase and nothing to remember.

changes.decision: Alert operations the moment payment lands and put the job on the schedule automatically.
changes.why: The hand-off that depended on someone remembering to tell operations is removed entirely.

changes.decision: One shared order record, confirmed by the driver’s scan, visible to managers and customers.
changes.why: The driver’s scan closes the loop at the point of collection, so the view is current without a phone call.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the WasteMart case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Quotes in minutes, terms included — the sales team picks the service and the quote is priced, with WasteMart’s standard terms attached automatically.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Accept and pay in one go — the customer receives the quote, accepts it, and gets a secure payment link straight away.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Operations, alerted instantly — the moment payment comes through, the job goes onto the schedule.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Planned, collected, confirmed — planners assign the truck and driver, and the driver confirms the collection with a scan.

cases.build: Designed and built by GEMIS’s own developers, under one roof, and supported by the same team since: quoting, payment links, scheduling, the driver app and order tracking are one system, not a design file handed to a third party. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.

resultsQualitative: A system that has grown with WasteMart for more than ten years.
Every order visible from quote to collection, for managers and customers alike.
resultsDesignedFor: Less admin between sale and collection
Faster payment, with no chasing for proof
Every job on time and visible to the customer

cases.name: SBS Waterproofing
cases.anonymised: A Cape Town waterproofing and roofing contractor
cases.timeline: Website and Google campaigns from 2014; the business system from 2015, extended since
cases.result: Still running the business on the system GEMIS built, more than ten years on
cases.resultNote: As stated in the case study
cases.imageAlt: SBS Waterproofing: the enquiry-to-project system on a laptop
problem: SBS Waterproofing keeps Cape Town’s roofs and walls dry. After GEMIS built its website and helped run its Google campaigns in 2014, enquiries started arriving faster than the business could keep track of them.

The off-the-shelf apps SBS tried did not fit the way a waterproofing contractor works: an enquiry becomes a site visit, a quote, a deposit, a scheduled job and a final invoice, with stock consumed along the way. Each step lived in a different tool, so leads were lost between them and nobody could see which jobs made money.
cases.findingsNote: There is no research report in the record for this project. The system was designed from how SBS already worked, and these are the facts that shaped the brief.
findings: Enquiries were arriving faster than anyone could keep track of them.
After a quote was accepted, the deposit and the accounting entry depended on someone remembering to raise them.
Nobody could see which jobs made money.
A generic package would have forced SBS to work the package’s way.

changes.decision: Make the enquiry the root record, captured once, with an SMS reference sent to the customer immediately.
changes.why: A single record that every call, email and appointment hangs off means nothing is lost between tools, and the customer has confirmation without a phone call.

changes.decision: Online quote acceptance raises the deposit invoice automatically and posts it into the accounting system.
changes.why: The hand-offs that leak time are the ones that rely on memory; automating them removes re-keying and the delay before a job can start.

changes.decision: Hold the costs with the sale and show the profit on every project.
changes.why: Management decisions should come from live job data rather than a reconstruction at year-end.

changes.decision: Design the system around SBS’s own pipeline, but general enough to serve other businesses.
changes.why: A system that fits the real sequence of work is the one the business keeps using; a general core lets it serve others without a rewrite.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the SBS Waterproofing case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Every enquiry, tracked — captured once, and the customer receives an SMS with a reference number straight away.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: From first call to the sale — new, contacted, site visit, quoted, won: every call, email and appointment on the enquiry.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Quote. Accept. Deposit. — when the customer accepts online, the deposit invoice follows automatically into accounting.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Profit, job by job — every project shows whether it made money, because the system holds the costs as well as the sale.

cases.build: GEMIS built the website and ran the Google campaigns first (2014), then designed and built the business system (2015) with its own developers, and has extended and supported it since — the same team on the website and on the system. The design was general enough that it later became ManaGEM. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.
resultsQualitative: More than ten years on, SBS still runs its business on the system GEMIS built.
SBS has grown many times over since the system went live (as stated in the case study).
The system became the foundation of ManaGEM, which about a dozen companies run on today.
resultsDesignedFor: No enquiry lost between tools; every lead followed through to a decision
Less office time spent on quotes, deposits and chasing paperwork
Management decisions made on profit per job rather than on turnover alone
cases.resultsNotRecorded: No figure is published for this project: formal usability testing or user-acceptance records are not in the repository, so none are claimed.

quote.text: By launching an online advertising campaign, we effectively doubled our turnover within 1 year. Since GEMIS created our new website, we're barely able to keep up with all the enquiries.

cases.name: HomeAssist
cases.industry: Insurance and home services — plumbing repairs
cases.timeline: Client since 2014; the system in use for more than ten years
cases.result: Every job across the country visible in one place, from first report to sign-off
cases.resultNote: As stated in the case study
cases.imageAlt: HomeAssist: the national job dashboard on a laptop and the plumber app on a phone
problem: A burst geyser is urgent for the homeowner, a claim for the insurer, and a dispatch problem for HomeAssist, which works with a national panel of plumbers. Each party needed something different: the homeowner wanted to report the problem in minutes and then know what was happening; the insurer needed the claim logged and the warranty position checked; the plumber needed to prove that each step of the repair met SANS standards; and HomeAssist needed to see every job in the country without phoning around.
Handled by phone and email, those needs pulled in different directions: updates meant calls, evidence meant paperwork, and warranty checks meant waiting on manufacturers.
cases.findingsNote: The record holds no research report for this project. The findings are the four parties a burst geyser involves and what each needed, as the case study states them.
findings: Homeowners and insurers reported the same problem through different channels.
Assigning a plumber from a national panel meant phoning around.
SANS compliance had to be proved after the fact, from paperwork.
Warranty positions and claim updates meant waiting on manufacturers and insurers.

changes.decision: One job record with two ways in: the homeowner reports online, or the insurer logs the claim.
changes.why: Every party then works from the same job rather than reconciling two versions of it by phone and email.

changes.decision: Assign the next available plumber near the job automatically.
changes.why: Dispatch by proximity and availability is faster than any phone round, and it does not wait on a person.

changes.decision: The plumber’s app captures a photograph at each step of the repair.
changes.why: Evidence captured where the work happens is complete and dated; evidence reconstructed afterwards is neither.

changes.decision: Link the system directly to insurers and manufacturers.
changes.why: The checks that used to be a phone call become part of the job’s own record, and the claim stays current.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the HomeAssist case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Two ways in. One system. — the homeowner reports online in minutes, or the insurer logs the claim; either way the job lands in one place.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: The nearest available plumber, found automatically — from a national panel, without a phone call.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Photo proof of SANS compliance — on site, the plumber photographs the work as each step is done.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Every job, nationwide, in one view — from first report to sign-off.

cases.build: Designed and built by GEMIS’s own developers — the intake, the dispatch, the customer messaging, the plumber app and the insurer and manufacturer links are one system — and supported by the same team for more than ten years. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.
resultsQualitative: GEMIS and HomeAssist have worked side by side for more than ten years, and the system remains in use.
Every job across the country visible in one place, from first report to sign-off.
resultsDesignedFor: Fewer phone calls for customers, plumbers and the office
Faster repairs, because dispatch no longer waits on a person
Compliance and warranty positions evidenced automatically
cases.resultsNotRecorded: No figure is published for this project: formal usability testing, user-acceptance records and usage figures are not in the repository, so none are claimed.

quote.text: The GEMIS team consistently met deadlines and delivered a solution that streamlined our operations, enhancing customer satisfaction and our market position.

cases.name: Trans Hex Group
cases.result: A report that took weeks became available on demand
cases.resultNote: As stated in the case study
cases.imageAlt: Trans Hex: the integrated management report on a laptop
problem: Trans Hex has mined diamonds for more than fifty years. At its Baken mine on the Lower Orange River, management needed one clear view across plant, mining, finance, security and people.
That view was pieced together in Excel from several sources, including SAP. It took weeks to assemble, errors crept in along the way, and by the time it was ready the month had moved on.
cases.findingsNote: The record holds no research report for this project. The brief was management’s own, and these are the facts the work had to answer.
findings: The existing information system was not reliable enough to build on.
Financial data was re-keyed from SAP into spreadsheets, and errors crept in.
A silent failure in an automated feed would only be discovered at month-end.
The management report lived outside the system, assembled by hand.

changes.decision: Stabilise the company’s own system before adding anything to it.
changes.why: A report is only as trustworthy as the system that holds its data; fixing the foundation first avoided building errors in.

changes.decision: Automate a daily SAP feed that runs on schedule, skips duplicates and logs every run.
changes.why: Loading the data once, automatically, removes the manual copy that introduced the errors.

changes.decision: Email the team if any run fails.
changes.why: Automation that fails loudly is safer than automation that fails quietly; a missing day is noticed the same morning.

changes.decision: Build the report into the system, with filters by mine and period and export to Excel and PDF.
changes.why: A report generated from the system is repeatable and current; one assembled beside it is neither.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the Trans Hex case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: SAP data, in every morning — the daily feed runs on schedule, skips duplicates, logs what it did, and emails the team if anything fails.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Budget against actual — gravel treated, carats, fleet availability and cost per carat, for the month and the year to date.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Any mine. Any period. — filter by mine, period or date range, then export to Excel or PDF.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Weekly. Forecast. Variance. — version two added weekly figures, forecasts, variances and live exchange rates.

cases.build: GEMIS’s own developers stabilised the company’s information system, automated the SAP feed and built the reporting into it, then delivered a second version with weekly figures, forecasts, variances, live exchange rates and mine groups. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.
resultsQualitative: A report that took weeks became available whenever it was needed (as stated in the case study).
A second version followed — evidence that the first was used and extended.
resultsDesignedFor: Fewer errors, because the data is loaded once and checked automatically
Management decisions on current figures rather than last month’s
One view across operations rather than one spreadsheet per source
cases.resultsNotRecorded: Time-saving figures beyond the case study’s own statement, and user-acceptance records, are not in the repository, so none are claimed.

cases.name: Sonke Gender Justice
cases.anonymised: A non-profit working across forty countries
cases.industry: Non-profit — gender-based violence and HIV prevention
cases.result: Donor reports built from data that has already been checked
cases.resultNote: As stated in the case study
cases.imageAlt: Sonke Gender Justice: the monitoring and evaluation dashboard on a laptop
problem: Sonke Gender Justice works to end gender-based violence and reduce the spread of HIV in forty countries across Africa. Every day its teams run workshops, dialogues and outreach, and funders ask a hard question: what difference did it make?

Answering it meant collecting evidence from sessions held far from any office, often without signal, and then proving that the numbers in a report corresponded to real activities. The problem was both capture and credibility.
cases.findingsNote: The record holds no research report for this project. The findings follow the question funders ask and the conditions under which the answer has to be gathered.
findings: Sessions happen far from any office, often without signal.
Funders need to trust that reported numbers correspond to real activities.
Country teams and leadership need different views of the same data.

changes.decision: An offline-first mobile app that syncs when there is signal.
changes.why: If capture depends on connectivity, the records that matter most — the remote ones — are the ones lost.

changes.decision: Nothing counts until an M&E officer has checked and approved it.
changes.why: An approval step between capture and counting is what makes every figure traceable to a session.

changes.decision: Role-based views: each role sees what it needs, and progress against targets is live by country and programme.
changes.why: One system can serve the field, the office and leadership if each sees its own slice rather than everything.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the Sonke Gender Justice case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Captured in the field. Even offline. — facilitators record each session on the mobile app; it syncs when there is signal.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Checked once, trusted everywhere — M&E officers approve what comes in, so every number traces to a real activity.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: The right view for every role — progress against targets by country and programme.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Donor reports, ready when you are — assembled from data that has already been checked.

cases.build: Designed and built by GEMIS’s own developers: the offline-first mobile app, the approval workflow, the role-based views and the donor reporting are one system. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.
resultsQualitative: Donor reports build from data that has already been checked (as stated in the case study).
resultsDesignedFor: Less time on paperwork for field and office teams
Donor reports built from verified data rather than reconstructed figures
Programme decisions made on current progress against targets
cases.resultsNotRecorded: Whether the system remains in use, usage figures, usability testing and user-acceptance records are not in the repository, so none are claimed.

cases.name: Tore’s Foundation
cases.client: Tore’s Foundation, for the University of Stellenbosch Business School
cases.anonymised: A schools debating programme across 24 Western Cape schools
cases.result: More time for debate, less time on admin
cases.resultNote: As stated in the case study
cases.imageAlt: Tore’s Foundation: live standings on a laptop and a coach’s expense claim on a phone
problem: Every week, Tore’s Foundation runs debating for more than 430 learners in 24 schools across the Western Cape. Behind every debate is a coach, a competition to run, and expenses and stipends to pay.
On paper, all of that was slow for everyone: results were compiled after the fact, standings lagged, and coaches’ claims had to be gathered, matched to sessions and paid one by one.
cases.findingsNote: The record holds no research report for this project. The findings follow the programme as it ran — on paper — before the platform.
findings: Fixtures, scores and claims were all on paper, and slow for everyone.
Standings lagged because results were compiled after the fact.
Coaches’ claims had to be gathered, matched to sessions and paid one by one.

changes.decision: One web platform for the debates and the admin behind them, rather than separate tools.
changes.why: The competition and the money are linked — claims are for sessions — so one system can verify what two cannot.

changes.decision: Capture results as each debate ends and update the standings straight away.
changes.why: Results captured at the event are trusted; results compiled later are questioned.

changes.decision: Claims from the phone with the receipt attached, checked against the sessions that ran, paid in one batch.
changes.why: Matching a claim to a recorded session makes payment both faster and verifiable.

cases.screensNote: Stills from the Tore’s Foundation case study video. The interfaces are illustrated for the video with sample data, not screen recordings of the product; every capability shown is one the system delivers. Before screens are not in the record.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Competitions set up in minutes — schools, rounds, motions and judges.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Results in, standings live — captured as each debate ends, through to the year-end final.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Coaches claim from their phone — pick the session, snap the receipt, submit.

screens.label: After
screens.caption: Checked, approved, paid — every claim matched to a session that ran, then one payment batch to finance.

cases.build: Designed and built by GEMIS’s own developers for the University of Stellenbosch Business School: one web platform for the competition and the money side of the programme. The work predates the studio’s current component-spec and handoff-session format, so none is recorded for it.
resultsQualitative: More time for debate, less time on admin (as stated in the case study).
Results and standings captured at the event, for 24 schools and more than 430 learners.
resultsDesignedFor: Standings and results trusted because they are captured at the event
Coaches paid faster, against sessions that verifiably ran
